summary:
I built the installable web app (addendum §4) on top of e0ae32c.

- **Icons and manifest:** an original logo mark (public/icons/mark.svg) and icons rendered from it by scripts/make-icons.ts. The manifest is wired into the layout with the Apple and theme meta tags.
- **Service worker (public/sw.js, hand-written):** precaches the app shell (manifest, icons, and an /offline page fetched without cookies). It serves /_next/static and /icons cache-first. Navigations to public pages go to the network first and fall back to /offline. It never answers /api (media included), signed-in pages, other origins, ranges or writes. It also handles push and notification clicks.
- **Offline state:** a useOnline hook, an offline banner in the shell, and an OfflineGuard wrapper. The job tray stops polling while offline.
- **Push server code (src/server/push):** VAPID configuration and pushStatus, subscriptions stored per session with an allowlist of push-service hosts, and notifyJobFinished. Notifications carry only {title, body, url, tag}, endpoints that return 404/410 are deleted, and it never throws.
- **Routes:** /api/push/public-key and /api/push/subscriptions (POST and DELETE). Logout and sign-out-everywhere remove subscriptions.
- **Settings:** one new "On this device" card with the install offer and the notifications toggle.
- **Headers:** next.config.ts serves sw.js and the manifest with the right headers.
- **Tests:** 48 new tests (30 unit, 18 integration); 169 pass in total.

docsNotes:
I added no env vars. VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY and VAPID_SUBJECT already existed in the "Installable web app" section of src/server/env.ts; I only added comments there. No accounts are needed: Web Push uses VAPID keys, not a vendor account.

INSTALL PER PLATFORM
The offer lives in Settings › On this device only. There is no popup: the registrar calls preventDefault() on beforeinstallprompt, so Chrome's own mini-infobar never shows.
- Android Chrome, Samsung Internet, desktop Chrome and Edge: an "Install Hushloom" button appears when the browser offers install. Otherwise the user installs from the browser menu (Install app / Add to Home screen).
- iPhone and iPad: in Safari (or another browser on iOS 16.4+), tap Share › Add to Home Screen.
- When running standalone, the card shows "Installed".
- Manifest: name and short_name Hushloom, start_url and scope "/", display standalone, background and theme #0f0a0d (ink-950), orientation any, categories entertainment and photo.
- Icons: 192 and 512 (any), 512 maskable, SVG, plus shortcuts for Make an image and Library.
- The layout sets apple-touch-icon (180), apple-mobile-web-app-capable and mobile-web-app-capable, status-bar style black, theme-color, color-scheme dark, and viewport-fit=cover (so the tab bar's safe-area padding works).
- Logo source is public/icons/mark.svg. Re-render the PNGs with `npx tsx scripts/make-icons.ts`.
- **Deployment:** standalone output does not include public/. The Dockerfile must copy public/ into the standalone folder, as playwright.config.ts now does.

SERVICE WORKER (public/sw.js, VERSION v1; bump VERSION to ship a new worker and drop old caches)
- Precached at install: /manifest.webmanifest, /icons/*, and /offline. /offline is fetched with credentials omitted and rendered without the shell, so it holds no account data; it is stored with only a Content-Type header. The /_next/static CSS and JS that /offline references are precached too.
- Cache-first: /_next/static/* (content-hashed) and /icons/*, capped at 250 entries.
- Network-first, with /offline as fallback: navigations to public pages (/, /explore, /templates, /creators, /policies, /generate, /offline). Page HTML is never stored.
- Never answered by the worker (the browser fetches as if it were absent): /api/* including /api/media, other origins, non-GET, Range requests, RSC/data fetches, and navigations to /collection, /projects, /studio, /train, /settings, /admin, /favorites, /pricing, /auth and /verify. Those show the browser's own offline error.
- shouldCache refuses any response that is private, no-store, not a 200, redirected or opaque, and anything outside /_next/static, /icons and the shell list.
- The browser's ordinary HTTP cache is separate from the worker. A signed media response (Cache-Control: private, max-age up to the link expiry, MEDIA_URL_TTL_S, default 300 s) can still be reused by the browser until the link expires; this is pre-existing behavior.
- Under `next dev` the worker registers as /sw.js?mode=dev: push only, no caching.
- Headers: sw.js is served with Cache-Control no-cache, Service-Worker-Allowed /, and CSP default-src 'self'. Registration uses updateViaCache none.
- Updates: skipWaiting on install and clients.claim on activate. A toast reads "Hushloom just updated. Reload when you're ready for the new version." when a new worker replaces an old one.

OFFLINE
- A slim banner under the top bar reads "You're offline. Nothing is queued; try again when you're back."
- The job tray pauses polling while offline and says so; it catches up when the connection returns.
- The /offline page has Try again (reloads the current address, works without JS), Go to Discover, and auto-reloads when back online.
- Nothing is queued offline: there is no background sync.

PUSH PAYLOAD POLICY
- Opt-in per account (user_preferences.notify_on_finish) and per device (a browser subscription).
- The payload is built by buildPushPayload(outcome, jobId) and contains only:
  - title: "Hushloom"
  - body: "Your creation is ready" / "A creation didn't finish" / "A creation was cancelled"
  - url: /collection/<jobId>
  - tag: job-<jobId>
- It never contains the prompt, template, model, media, handle, email or failure detail.
- The worker shows only those fields, with same-origin URLs only, icon /icons/icon-192.png and badge /icons/badge-96.png.
- Sent with aes128gcm encryption, TTL 12 h, urgency normal, only to devices whose session is still valid.
- 404/410 responses delete the subscription; other failures set failed_at and keep it.
- Logs carry ids and counts only. Endpoints are capability URLs and are never logged or audited.

SUBSCRIPTIONS
- POST /api/push/subscriptions upserts on endpoint and ties the row to the current session id. It returns 503 push_disabled without VAPID keys, 401 when signed out, 422 for bad input, and is rate-limited to 60 per hour per user.
- Endpoints must be https on a known push service: fcm.googleapis.com, android.googleapis.com, updates.push.services.mozilla.com, *.push.apple.com, *.notify.windows.com. This prevents SSRF.
- DELETE removes by endpoint, only the caller's own rows.
- POST /api/auth/logout removes that session's rows. Deleting a session row also cascades (verified in tests).
- Sign out everywhere, account deletion and admin suspension all remove every row (via destroyAllSessions).
- After a later sign-in, the browser re-binds its existing subscription to the new session once per tab session.
- Audit actions: push.subscribe (new device only) and push.unsubscribe.

VAPID SETUP
- Generate once per deployment with `npx web-push generate-vapid-keys`.
- Set VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY and VAPID_SUBJECT (mailto: or https:; Apple rejects localhost) in the secret store. Never commit them.
- Rotating the pair invalidates existing subscriptions; users turn notifications on again.
- Without keys the toggle is disabled with "Push is not configured on this server." This is not a demo mode: nothing pretends to send.

UNVERIFIED
- Real push delivery.
- Real device install on Android, desktop and iOS, and iOS push.
- The worker under a production Next build.
- The update toast.
- notificationclick and pushsubscriptionchange.
